solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Artist describes tip to sketch a flower

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so the painter's name goes around the next piece

parts.note: Salvador Dali, the Spanish surrealist painter

indicators.note: the tip to a word here is its final letter, the end of the pencil stroke

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter outlines a bloom, with some advice on how to finish the sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip to sketch' gives H, the last letter, which DALI wraps round ('describes'), before A is added.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a garden plant with showy blooms, an example of the broader term in the clue.

clue.text: Lecturer with unusual laugh snorted on extended journey

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for a learner or lecturer

indicators.note: an unusual version of a word has its letters in an odd order, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written, part of the jumbled material
taken as written, the word the laugh is snorted on to, joining the jumbled material

explanation.surface: A lecturer with a strange snorting laugh during a long trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snorted on' only ties the two words together; 'unusual' rearranges the laugh along with the word on, so both sets of letters are jumbled as one pool after the lecturer.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-haul travel covers great distances, such as intercontinental flights, so the term describes a lengthy trip.

clue.text: Catch Romeo finally leaving lover in opposite direction

indicators.note: going in the opposite direction means the remaining word is read from back to front
something leaving at the end means the last occurrence of the letter is dropped

parts.note: a lover is a romantic partner
R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Romeo walks away from his lover at last, heading the other way.
explanation.walkthrough: PARTNER loses its final R ('Romeo finally leaving') to give PARTNE, which turned round ('in opposite direction') gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensnare someone is to catch them out by trickery; both verbs mean trapping.

clue.text: Comprehensive surprisingly taken with outsiders from borstal

indicators.note: the outsiders of a word are its first and last letters
surprisingly signals the letters turn up in an unexpected order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A comprehensive school that surprisingly took in outsiders from a youth prison.
explanation.walkthrough: A borstal was a former British youth detention centre. 'Comprehensive' poses as the British state school but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A blanket ban or policy covers everything, so it is all-embracing or wide-ranging.

clue.text: Depression starts to lessen after resizing bust

parts.note: a col is a dip or pass between two mountain peaks

indicators.note: the starts to several words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: Feeling low, a woman hopes the downturn will ease once her bust is resized.
explanation.definitionFit: Police slang: to bust someone is to arrest them, and to collar them means the same nab.

clue.text: Worry about key Frenchman getting disease

indicators.note: about here signals going round backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: to nag is to worry or pester someone
G is one of the musical keys
Rene is a typical French man's name

explanation.surface: A Frenchman fretting over something important who ends up seriously ill.
explanation.walkthrough: NAG turned 'about' gives GAN.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a condition in which body tissue dies, a specific example of an illness.

clue.text: Body of water in the past overrun by sole mostly

indicators.note: being overrun by something means it surrounds and swamps the other piece
mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: sole means single or lone
ago means in the past, as in long ago

explanation.surface: A body of water once teeming with sole fish.
explanation.walkthrough: LONE cut short ('mostly') gives LON, which surrounds AGO ('overrun by'). 'sole' looks like the fish but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallow stretch of sea cut off by a reef or sandbar is one kind of watery expanse.

clue.text: Coastal region enlightened the foremost of travellers speaking

parts.note: lit means lighted up, illuminated

indicators.note: the foremost of a word is its leading letter

parts.note: oral means spoken, done by speaking

explanation.surface: An enlightened travel leader speaks about the seaside area.
explanation.definitionFit: The technical term for the shore zone of a sea or lake, the strip by the coast.

clue.text: Hot lady's stifled by onset of travel sickness

indicators.note: being stifled by something means being smothered inside it
the onset of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: mal is sickness, as in mal de mer, seasickness
her is the possessive pronoun, the lady's

explanation.surface: A woman feels hot and smothered as travel sickness sets in.
explanation.walkthrough: The sickness word is French for illness, familiar from mal de mer; 'stifled by' wraps the travel letter and sickness round the lady's pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: Thermal means relating to heat, so a thermal spring is a hot one.

clue.text: Section of drive perhaps following trail

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
to trail is to lag behind

explanation.surface: Part of a car journey spent following a trail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drive' suggests a journey, but it is a driveway, paved in slabs. Blue Flag is also an award for a clean beach, part of the hidden theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagstone is one paving slab, so one piece of a paved driveway, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Take to the street around mid-morning? It's what a cleaner may do

definitions.text: It's what a cleaner may do

indicators.note: around means the first piece is placed on both sides of the next

parts.note: to rise up is to revolt, taking protests onto the street

indicators.note: mid- picks out the central letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A cleaner heads out onto the street mid-morning to work.
explanation.walkthrough: N, the middle of 'morning', sits inside RISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cleaning will wash things through with clean water, so swilling is a cleaner's job.

clue.text: Wallbanger on ice which has you flat on your back?

definitions.text: Wallbanger on ice which has you flat on your back?

parts.words: Wallbanger on ice which has you flat on your back?
parts.note: the cocktail Harvey Wallbanger served on ice could knock you flat, but the real picture is a racing sled ridden lying face up, banging the walls of an icy chute

explanation.surface: A strong cocktail on the rocks that leaves the drinker flat on their back.
explanation.walkthrough: A Harvey Wallbanger is a vodka cocktail; here the 'wallbanger' is a sled ricocheting off the walls of an icy track.
explanation.definitionFit: This light sled is ridden feet first, lying supine, down an ice run, often grazing its banked sides.

clue.text: Rotten person misdirected small swimmer at Gala perhaps

indicators.note: sent the wrong way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a dab is a small flatfish
Gala is a variety of eating fruit from an orchard

explanation.surface: A swimming gala where a small entrant is sent the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gala' suggests a swimming event, but it is a type of apple.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: one corrupt individual who spoils the group, like a rotting fruit spoiling the barrel.

clue.text: Avidly consume wine and spirit in retirement

indicators.note: retiring is drawing back, so the words are read backwards

parts.note: red is a type of wine
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: A retiree drinking wine and spirits with gusto.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang you can 'murder' a pint or a curry, meaning devour or drink it eagerly.

clue.text: Supermarket's outside Paris according to Cockney wanting cheese?

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its first and last letters
Cockney Londoners famously drop their aitches

parts.note: Paris Hilton, the American hotel heiress

explanation.surface: A Cockney shopper outside a supermarket in Paris wants some cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: ST is the outside of 'Supermarket'; the Cockney says 'ILTON. 'Paris' looks like the French city but is the celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong English blue-veined variety, a specific example of the general foodstuff.

clue.text: Ancient character, with little energy entering incline becomes tense

parts.note: tau is a letter of the ancient Greek alphabet

indicators.note: entering means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: to incline is to tend
E is the abbreviation for energy, little meaning abbreviated

explanation.surface: A historical figure, low on energy, finds that leaning over makes him stiff.
explanation.definitionFit: To tighten or stiffen is to tense; the past form matches the answer, as in 'muscles tensed'.

clue.text: Classical art graduate's inside playing chap performing in gig?

indicators.note: inside means the earlier pieces are placed within the next

parts.note: on means playing, as an actor on stage
ars is Latin, the classical language, for art
MA is a Master of Arts graduate

explanation.surface: A classics graduate playing in a band at a gig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gig' suggests a concert, but it is a light rowing boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A gig is a long narrow rowing boat, so a man performing in one is a rower.

clue.text: John finally settled in base, made ready for action

indicators.note: in means the pieces are put inside the outer word

parts.note: a bed is a base or foundation, as in a riverbed or flower bed
john is slang for a toilet, or loo

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of a word

explanation.surface: John eventually settles in at base, ready for action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like a man's name but is American slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops are blooded when given their first taste of combat, initiating them for battle.

clue.text: Dental problem needing brace in public is a source of embarrassment

indicators.note: in means the pair goes inside the word for public

parts.note: overt means open or public
a brace is a pair, and bi- is the prefix for two

indicators.note: a source of a word is where it starts, its opening letter

explanation.surface: Wearing a dental brace in public is embarrassing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brace' looks like orthodontics but means a pair, BI.
explanation.definitionFit: An orthodontic fault where the upper front teeth overlap the lower ones too far.

clue.text: Shrub calamitous girl carries back to hers over motorway

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Calamity Jane, the Wild West frontierswoman

indicators.note: the back to a word is its final letter

parts.note: M1 is the British motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: A disaster-prone woman gives a lift home to a friend along the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' simply places the end of 'hers' before the motorway; M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing plant with fragrant white or yellow flowers, an example of a woody bush.

clue.text: Friend opposed to overpowering constant note

indicators.note: one piece overpowering another takes its place

parts.note: Quakers belong to the Religious Society of Friends
k is a common symbol for a constant in science
v stands for versus, meaning against or opposed to

explanation.surface: A pacifist friend stands against an overbearing, unchanging regime.
explanation.walkthrough: In QUAKER, the K ('constant') is replaced by V ('opposed to').
explanation.definitionFit: A musical symbol worth half a crotchet, an eighth note, is one kind of written note.

clue.text: Money abroad raised to examine fabric

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: the lev is the currency of Bulgaria
to vet is to check or examine

explanation.surface: Foreign money raised to inspect some cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: LEV goes up to give VEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft woven cloth with a dense pile, an example of a material.

clue.text: People hearing opera periodically re-enacted on German estate, say

indicators.note: on, in an across clue, means the second part comes after the first

parts.note: Audi is a German car maker, whose models include estate cars

indicators.note: periodically picks every other letter

explanation.surface: An opera re-enacted on a German country estate.
explanation.walkthrough: ENCE is the even letters of 're-enacted'. 'estate' looks like land but is a station wagon car.
explanation.definitionFit: The listeners or spectators at a performance are the assembled crowd.

clue.text: Long distance runner partial to one bun a day when building up

indicators.note: in a down clue, building up means reading upwards, backwards
partial means only part of the phrase is taken

explanation.surface: A marathon runner who is fond of a bun a day while training.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters EBUNAD, inside 'one bun a day', read upwards. 'runner' is a river, not an athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is a runner in crosswords, and this one flows nearly three thousand kilometres across Europe.

clue.text: Ally excited to be entertained by old King

indicators.note: being entertained by someone means being held within, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: Old King Cole, the nursery-rhyme monarch
up means excited or worked up

explanation.surface: An ally thrilled to be hosted by an elderly monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: To ally things is to join them, so to link or pair them together.

clue.text: Bowling erratic line and length, openers given warning

indicators.note: the openers of several words are their first letters, and openers is also cricket's term for first batsmen

explanation.surface: A cricket commentary: erratic bowling to the openers, who are warned.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarm or a ringing signal alerts people, so it gives notice of danger.

clue.text: French woman keeps reading, for example, new series of kid's books

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside

parts.note: Mme is the abbreviation for Madame
reading is one of the three Rs

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman continues reading a new set of children's books.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Roger Hargreaves's children's picture-book range, featuring Mr Happy, Mr Tickle and others.

clue.text: Some here go along with this blasted shouting

definitions.text: Some here go along with this

indicators.note: something shouted is heard rather than seen, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: blasted means blown, past tense of blow

explanation.surface: Someone loudly cursing at others who go along with it.
explanation.walkthrough: The theme: many answers in this grid can follow the colour, as in lagoon, rinse, Stilton and murder.
explanation.definitionFit: The colour pairs with a dozen solutions in this grid, for instance blue Danube, blue velvet and bluebottle.

clue.text: Enjoy getting thousand pounds in contest by no means over

indicators.note: in means the money goes inside the competition word

parts.note: a bee is a contest, as in a spelling bee
K is a thousand, and a grand means a thousand pounds

indicators.note: over signals turning the word round

parts.note: none means not at all, as in none the wiser

explanation.surface: A thousand-pound prize in a competition is no fun when it's lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns round the word for 'by no means', giving ENON.
explanation.definitionFit: To relish or be fond of something is to find pleasure in it, the same as enjoying it.

clue.text: One's drunk from the French dry earlier with bad smell

indicators.note: earlier places the piece before the next one

parts.note: BO is body odour
TT means teetotal, so dry
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A drunk once dry, with a nasty smell from a French bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's drunk from' reads as a person who has been drinking, but it describes the vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinking vessel is a container you drink from, glass or plastic.
